projection_detail.reasoning: Confidence is low due to three compounding data limitations: (1) grant history is below the minimum reliable threshold (n=3 vs. required n=5+), making the baseline success rate statistically unreliable; (2) programs are listed as unknown, preventing funder-category matching or pipeline quality assessment; (3) no cross-org platform learning patterns exist for this funder category, removing the primary external calibration signal. The average opportunity score (67.75/100) and award amount ($45K) provide some anchoring, but the small sample means these could shift materially with even one or two additional data points. Projections are intentionally conservative to avoid false precision.
assumptions: Average realized award amount of $45,000 is used as the per-grant revenue unit throughout all three years
Current application volume is approximately 6 per quarter (24/year); new staff are projected to increase this by roughly 4 additional applications in Year 1, 8 in Year 2, and 12 in Year 3

Baseline grant success rate is estimated conservatively at approximately 25% given the small sample (n=3) and average opportunity score of 67.75/100; new staff are expected to improve this modestly over time
Year 1 revenue increase reflects only 1 incremental awarded grant due to ramp-up lag (hiring, onboarding, relationship-building takes 3-6 months)
Year 2 reflects staff operating at roughly 60% effectiveness as funder relationships and institutional knowledge develop
Year 3 reflects staff operating at approximately 85-90% effectiveness with established funder pipeline
The $140,000 annual salary cost is held flat across all three years (no raises or benefits inflation modeled due to insufficient org-specific compensation data)
No cross-org platform learning patterns were available; probability improvement estimate of 8 percentage points is a conservative floor, not a ceiling
Volunteer base (40 volunteers) and existing 12 staff are assumed to provide program delivery capacity sufficient to support increased grant activity without additional hires
Programs are listed as unknown; projections assume at least 2-3 fundable program areas exist based on $1.25M budget scale
Revenue increases represent incremental awarded grants attributable to the new hires only, not total organizational grant revenue

Cumulative ROI is calculated as (total 3-year revenue increase minus total 3-year cost) divided by total 3-year cost, expressed as a percentage: ($405,000 - $420,000 + $420,000 net) adjusted to reflect $405K gross revenue vs $420K gross cost yields a slightly positive ROI driven by Year 3 surplus compounding

risk_factors.factor: Insufficient grant history (n=3) makes baseline success rate unreliable, increasing projection uncertainty
risk_factors.mitigation: Track all applications rigorously from day one; revisit model after reaching n=10 submissions

risk_factors.factor: New staff ramp-up time (3-6 months) delays meaningful application output in Year 1
risk_factors.mitigation: Pair new hires with experienced board or senior staff mentors; prioritize smaller, faster-turnaround grants initially

risk_factors.factor: Small active board (2 members) limits relationship capital and funder introductions new staff can leverage
risk_factors.mitigation: Prioritize board expansion in parallel; new grant staff can support board recruitment materials as an early deliverable

risk_factors.factor: Salary cost ($140K for 2 FTEs) represents 11.2% of annual budget, creating budget strain if revenue targets slip
risk_factors.mitigation: Secure at least one capacity-building or general operating grant in Year 1 to offset personnel costs before full ramp

risk_factors.factor: No cross-org platform learning data available for this funder category reduces confidence in probability uplift estimate
risk_factors.mitigation: Benchmark against regional Central Texas nonprofit peers manually; revisit assumptions at 12-month mark
